zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## Fed上修通膨預測，2年期美債殖利率跳升15個基點

Fed週三維持利率不變，但官員大幅上修通膨預測，支持今年繼續升息的人數也增加，短天期美債隨之下跌。2年期殖利率上升15個基點至4.20%，10年期上升6個基點至4.49%，兩者利差收窄9個基點至29個基點；30年期則持平於4.93%。

18位官員中有9位預期今年至少升息1碼，其中6位預期升息2碼以上。再加上主席Kevin Warsh強調必須將通膨拉回2%，這次維持3.50%至3.75%的決定，更像是在升息路徑上暫停觀察。會前公布的零售銷售也優於預期，顯示需求尚未明顯轉弱，難以單靠經濟降溫消化價格衝擊。

10年期美債殖利率上升，幾乎全由實質殖利率推動。儘管原油當天反彈，通膨補償仍下降；市場一方面看好荷姆茲海峽石油運輸恢復，另一方面也預期Fed維持緊縮。股市下跌、美元走強、波動率上升，但長債殖利率持平，具備明確再融資需求的發行人仍取得買盤。這次調整在政策敏感的曲線前端最劇烈，其他市場的反應則較不一致。

## 通膨預測、零售支出與美債曲線

5年期美債殖利率上升11個基點至4.27%，介於2年期的15個基點及10年期的6個基點之間。2年與30年期利差收窄15個基點至73個基點。相較之下，蝶式利差變化較小：2s5s10s上升1個基點至−15個基點，2s10s30s下降3個基點至−15個基點。賣壓主要沿著前端與中段展開，並非集中在單一天期。

從較長區間看，2年期殖利率一週上升7個基點、一個月上升11個基點，30年期卻仍分別下降10及19個基點。10年期也較一週前低6個基點、較一個月前低10個基點。週三逆轉了前一日的美債漲勢，尚未抹去長端殖利率近一個月的降幅。

10年期實質殖利率跳升9個基點至2.23%，損益兩平通膨率則下降3個基點至2.26%。5年期實質殖利率上升16個基點至1.96%，7年期上升13個基點至2.09%；20及30年期漲幅較小，分別上升5及3個基點至2.55%與2.73%。投資人提高了持有中期債券所要求的實質報酬，長期通膨補償卻同步下降。

FOMC於美東時間14:00一致決議維持3.50%至3.75%。18位官員中，半數預期2026年至少升息1碼，其中6位預期升息2碼以上；另外9位預期持平或降息。Warsh未提交個人利率路徑，因此點陣圖沒有直接呈現他的預測。不過，他反覆重申2%的通膨目標，同時表示將檢討Fed的溝通、資產負債表及整體通膨框架。

新的經濟預測說明了市場為何在意這份點陣圖。2026年通膨預測中位數從2.7%上修至3.6%，核心通膨預測也從2.7%上修至3.3%。成長預期由2.4%降至2.2%，失業率預估卻從4.4%降至4.3%。這意味經濟可以放緩，但官員並不預期勞動市場會明顯轉弱，替通膨壓力提供緩衝。記者會後，交易員完整反映10月前升息，9月也已被視為可能時點。

Warsh規劃的資產負債表檢討，另外增添利率市場的不確定性。工作小組將評估充裕準備金制度，以及Fed總額$6.7兆持債的組成。量化緊縮已在2025年底停止，Fed自去年12月起每月買進約$400億國庫券，以緩解短期利率壓力。這次並未宣布新的縮表時程，未來對準備金供給與國庫券需求有何影響，仍待觀察。

會前公布的5月零售及餐飲銷售成長0.9%至$7,637億，優於預期的0.6%；4月增幅則從0.5%下修至0.4%。銷售年增6.9%，其中零售業月增1.0%，非實體通路年增12.2%。這份數據顯示，儘管較高融資成本已壓抑住宅市場，消費支出仍有韌性。

油市則提供相反的通膨訊號。荷姆茲海峽運輸可望恢復，使原油在過去一週大跌，10年期損益兩平通膨率也繼續下降。不過，週三庫存數據顯示近期供應仍緊：商業原油庫存減少830萬桶，戰略石油儲備下降890萬桶，煉油廠每日投入量升至1,719.2萬桶。即使市場預期未來供應恢復，眼前的庫存下降仍使油價容易受新干擾影響。

國庫券殖利率也逐漸反映較高的政策利率路徑。13週上升5個基點至3.77%，26週上升11個基點至3.91%，52週上升14個基點至3.98%；極短天期僅變動1個基點。愈往一年期、升幅愈大，與未來升息預期更一致，並不像是眼前現金突然短缺。

$690億119天期國庫券得標貼現利率3.670%，換算投資利率3.767%。投標倍數2.87，最高得標利率的配售比例為11.86%。在$684.59億競爭性標售得標金額中，間接投標人獲配$362.82億，直接投標人$34.86億，交易商$286.91億。資料沒有提供前次標售或同時點發行前交易報價，難以進一步比較定價；6月23日交割時才會產生對應的資金移轉。

## 融資交易持續，優質借款人拿到較好條件

HDFC Bank發行$7.5億5年期美元債，利差為美債加90個基點，創該行新券最低紀錄。訂單超過$13億，讓最終利差比初步指引收斂30個基點。該行2024年2月前次$7.5億發債的3及5年期利差，分別為95及108個基點；這次同樣5年期的定價，較前次低18個基點。

今年HDFC股價已下跌21%，董事長辭職也引發公司治理疑慮。印度央行表示，沒有發現重大操守問題。儘管股票承壓，債券訂單仍顯示，投資人願意提供資金給這家印度最大民營銀行。

交通運輸業也能取得資金。雅典國際機場首度發行歐元債，透過7年期債券籌得€5億，利差為中期交換利率加98個基點。葡萄牙航空TAP則開始就擬發行的€3億5年期投機級債券與投資人接觸，同時政府正推動出售49.9%股權。今年航空與機場業發債超過$105億，創2021年以來上半年最高。2020至2021年發行的航空業債券中，逾$220億會在5至7年後到期，因此替換疫情時期融資，是目前發債的重要需求。TAP仍處於初步接觸階段，與雅典機場已完成的交易不同。

聯想以股價表現支持零息可轉債發行，籌得$20億，2033年到期，轉換溢價47.5%，落在先前推介的40%至50%區間。資金將用於再融資及股票回購，包括以本金的293.2%買回既有2029年可轉債。原持有人、可轉債專業投資人及長期型基金都有參與。公司省下現金利息，但未來仍可能面臨股權稀釋。

Nassau County Tobacco Settlement Corp.的情況與成功再融資形成鮮明對比。公司未支付6月初到期的$3,600萬款項，成為總額約$800億、以菸草和解金收入支持的市政債市場中首宗違約。捲菸出貨量長期下降，侵蝕了20多年前發行債券所仰賴的現金流；未付款消息也拖累同類債券。問題源於擔保收入持續走弱，並非週三美債殖利率變動造成。

ECB另提出AI使用的營運風險。拉加德表示，應用擴大可能使金融曝險更集中，也增加網路攻擊弱點。ECB已用重大網攻情境測試109家銀行，並計畫致函執行長，要求檢視韌性及必要投資。這是監理關注與未來成本，尚非已發生的AI相關信用損失。

信用ETF隨股市與美債下跌：LQD跌0.32%，HYG跌0.37%，JNK跌0.38%。若要判斷個別借款人的條件，HDFC與雅典機場的訂單、聯想可轉債條款及菸草債違約，提供的資訊比基金的小幅波動更具體。

## 歐洲與日本仍有各自的政策難題

即使油價回落，歐元區的通膨仍相當廣泛。5月整體通膨年增率確認為3.2%，高於前期3.0%；核心通膨從2.2%升至2.6%。服務價格漲幅達3.5%，對整體年增率貢獻1.61個百分點，能源貢獻0.98個百分點。投資人仍預期ECB至少再升息25個基點，使存款利率達2.5%。

ECB官員警告，基礎設施受損、庫存重建與工資反應，可能讓能源漲價的影響持續。央行工資追蹤指標預示下半年薪資年增2.6%，遠低於2024年5.2%的高峰，但仍高於上半年。現貨油價下降，讓官員有更多時間觀察；服務價格與工資數據則使他們無法宣布衝擊已結束。

瑞典央行連續第6次會議維持1.75%，但提高了對2026年稍晚升息可能性的評估。基礎通膨偏低、經濟活動弱於正常水準，5月失業率也達9.4%。儘管如此，其預測利率路徑仍在2027年第4季達到2%。這次決議維持觀望，對中期利率的看法卻上移。

英國5月整體通膨維持2.8%，沒有升至市場預估的3%，10年期英國公債殖利率因此下降5個基點至4.74%，為2個月低點。但服務通膨上升至3.7%，高於預期。英國央行6月18日料將維持3.75%，後續是否能降息，仍取決於服務物價。

日本6月16日升息後，仍是全球投資人的關注焦點。長天期日債殖利率小幅走高；6月17日調查的44位經濟學家中，有90%預期12月前再升息，最多人選擇12月，其次為10月，預估本輪最終利率的中位數則升至1.75%。日本央行計畫從2027年4月停止主動縮減每月購債，有助穩定供給預期，但日本投資人面對的本地利率與公債殖利率，已比這次決議前高。

中國則調整短期資金管理的方式。人民銀行表示，未來將朝隔夜政策利率架構轉型，把市場借款成本周邊的利率走廊由70個基點縮窄至50個基點，並設立讓外國官方機構以政府債券取得人民幣流動性的機制。這些改變涉及資金市場架構，也提高中國公債作為擔保品的用途；週三並非一般的政策利率調整。

## 南非通膨低於預期，巴西收盤後降息

南非5月消費者物價年增率由4.0%升至4.5%，為近2年最高，卻低於預估4.7%；核心通膨從3.6%升至3.8%。合約反映11月前累計升息預期由34個基點降至25個基點，隱含政策利率高點7.25%。即使通膨仍高於央行3%目標，低於預期的結果仍使利率市場稍獲舒緩。

巴西央行在紐約時間17:00固定收益市場收盤後，將Selic利率下調25個基點至14.25%，已連續第3次降息。央行同時警告，經濟成長與通膨均已加速，財政刺激可能增加價格壓力。通膨高於容忍區間，預期也高於3%目標。將達標時程延至2028年初，使這次降息有空間，但政策說明並未排除8月暫停降息。

美元隨美國短期利率上升，使未避險外債的負擔加重。日圓也貶至約每$1兌¥160.80，市場再度關注干預與利差交易平倉風險。日本當局從4月底至5月底曾投入創紀錄的¥11.73兆，因此投資人對匯率突然逆轉保持警覺。不過，週三並未出現明確的美元資金市場凍結。

EMB在美元利率上升之際下跌0.40%。南非利率定價的反應，以及巴西稍晚公布的決議，說明基金走勢無法代表每一個本地政策或主權信用變化。

## 股市下跌、美元走強，半導體股逆勢上漲

實質殖利率上升，使S&P 500下跌1.21%、Nasdaq 100下跌0.99%，VIX則跳升12.37%至18.44。費城半導體指數逆勢上漲1.38%。晶片股連續幾天大幅波動，這次表現是重要例外，但沒有改變整體股市下跌的事實。

美元指數上漲0.55%至100.09，與相對政策預期轉變的方向一致。WTI反彈0.97%至$76.79，布蘭特上漲0.75%至$79.55；兩者一週仍跌約14.5%，一個月約跌27%。油價單日反彈與大量庫存消耗，顯示近期供應風險仍在；10年期損益兩平通膨率下降，則表示美債投資人仍反映未來荷姆茲海峽重新開放的部分效益。

儘管美元與實質殖利率走高，黃金仍上漲0.65%至$4,358.90，但一個月累計下跌4.32%。單日漲幅不足以判定投資人持倉的單一動機。放眼各市場，最一致的變化是美國政策敏感殖利率與美元上行；油價及半導體股沒有跟隨大盤方向。

## 週四數據與標售接踵而至，之後市場休市

6月18日美東時間08:30將公布初領失業救濟金人數及費城Fed製造業指數，前值分別為22.9萬人及−0.4。Fed上修通膨預測、交易員開始反映10月前升息後，這將是第一批新公布的勞動與工廠活動資料。

各國央行決策也集中在週四：瑞士於美東時間03:30、挪威04:00、英國07:00公布結果，三者預期均維持利率；調查則預期印尼與菲律賓央行各升息25個基點。表決與政策說明，以及匯率反應，將呈現各國如何看待能源衝擊及其部分逆轉。

紐約固定收益市場17:00收盤後公布的消息，則已成為下一個亞洲交易時段的參考。台灣連續第9季維持利率2%，但政策語氣偏鷹，並將2026年成長預測從7.28%上修至9.45%，通膨預測為1.91%。紐西蘭第1季經濟成長0.8%，前一季則上修至0.5%；交換市場反映7月8日紐西蘭央行升息1碼的機率為80%。這些消息不能用來解釋已完成的美國收盤，卻會進入下一輪區域市場的判斷。

6月18日美東時間11:30，財政部將標售$700億4週與$750億8週國庫券，13:00續發$240億、票息1.25%的5年期TIPS。Fed決議後的投標情況、TIPS定價及短期資金利率，將有助判斷需求，之後6月19日固定收益市場全天休市。
zh-TW.methodology_note: 除非另有註明，市場水準均以紐約收盤為準。

overall_summary.headline: Fed升息支持度提高，2年期美債殖利率跳升15個基點
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Fed維持利率不變，卻將2026年通膨預測從2.7%上修至3.6%。18位官員中有9位預期今年至少升息1次，其中6位預期升息2次以上。2年期美債殖利率上升15個基點至4.20%，10年期上升6個基點至4.49%，30年期持平於4.93%。10年期實質殖利率上升9個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點。

5月零售銷售成長0.9%，優於預期0.6%，使Fed更有理由暫緩降息。Warsh首場記者會後，交易員完整反映10月前升息。他規劃檢討Fed溝通與總額$6.7兆的資產負債表，增加國庫券需求方面的不確定性，但尚未宣布新的縮表路徑。

HDFC Bank以自身新券最低利差發行$7.5億5年期債，雅典機場完成歐元債首發，聯想則籌得$20億零息可轉債。另一端，Nassau County Tobacco Settlement Corp.未支付$3,600萬款項，反映借款人條件差異仍大。歐元區通膨擴大，南非物價則低於預期；巴西在紐約收盤後降息。股市下跌、美元走強，但半導體股逆勢上漲。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Fed Forecasts Send Two-Year Treasury Yields Up 15 Basis Points

The Federal Reserve left rates unchanged on Wednesday, but a marked increase in officials' inflation forecasts and support for further tightening sent short-dated Treasuries sharply lower. The 2-year yield rose 15 basis points to 4.20%; the 10-year added 6 to 4.49%, narrowing the gap between them by 9 basis points to 29. The 30-year yield held at 4.93%.

Nine of 18 officials projected at least one quarter-point increase this year, including six who saw two or more. That split, along with Chair Kevin Warsh's emphasis on returning inflation to 2%, made the unchanged 3.50%-3.75% target range look like a pause rather than the end of restraint. Retail sales had already beaten forecasts before the decision, leaving less evidence that demand was weakening enough to absorb the price shock without more policy help.

The rise in Treasury yields came almost entirely through real rates at the 10-year point. Inflation compensation fell despite a daily rebound in crude, showing that investors could recognize the prospect of restored oil flows through Hormuz while expecting a more restrictive Fed. Equities fell, the dollar strengthened and volatility rose. Yet the long bond was unchanged, and credit issuers with clear refinancing needs still found buyers. The repricing was forceful at the policy end of the curve, with a more uneven response elsewhere.

## Inflation Forecasts, Retail Spending and the Curve

The 5-year Treasury yield rose 11 basis points to 4.27%, against the 2-year's 15-basis-point increase and the 10-year's 6-basis-point rise. The 2s30s spread narrowed 15 basis points to 73. Curve butterflies changed much less: 2s5s10s rose 1 basis point to -15 and 2s10s30s fell 3 to -15. The selloff was concentrated across the front and belly rather than one isolated maturity.

The shorter end also looked different over longer periods. The 2-year yield was 7 basis points higher over a week and 11 higher over a month; the 30-year was still lower by 10 and 19. The 10-year remained 6 basis points below its level a week earlier and 10 below a month earlier. Wednesday reversed the previous session's broad rally without erasing the longer decline in long yields.

The 10-year real yield jumped 9 basis points to 2.23%, while its breakeven inflation rate fell 3 to 2.26%. Five-year real yields rose 16 basis points to 1.96% and 7-year yields gained 13 to 2.09%. In contrast, 20- and 30-year real yields increased 5 and 3 basis points, to 2.55% and 2.73%. The market raised the real-rate cost of holding intermediate Treasuries even as its longer-run inflation compensation declined.

The FOMC voted unanimously at 14:00 ET to hold its target range at 3.50%-3.75%. Half of the 18 officials projected at least a quarter-point increase in 2026; six saw two or more, and the other nine expected no move or a cut. Warsh did not submit a personal rate path, leaving his own view outside the dots. He repeatedly committed to the 2% inflation objective while saying he would review the Fed's communications, balance sheet and broader inflation framework.

The new forecasts explain why traders paid attention to the dots. Median 2026 inflation was raised to 3.6% from 2.7%, and the core forecast to 3.3% from 2.7%. Expected growth slipped to 2.2% from 2.4%, but projected unemployment was lowered to 4.3% from 4.4%. That combination allows slower growth while giving officials little expected labor-market relief from the inflation problem. After the press conference, traders fully priced an increase by October, with September already seen as a likely meeting.

Warsh's planned balance-sheet review added a separate source of uncertainty for rates investors. A task force will assess the ample-reserves system and the composition of the Fed's $6.7 trillion portfolio. Quantitative tightening ended in late 2025, and the Fed has bought about $40 billion of bills a month since December to ease pressure in short-term rates. The review announced no new runoff schedule; its eventual effect on reserve supply and bill demand remains open.

May retail and food-services sales rose 0.9% to $763.7 billion before the Fed decision, beating the 0.6% estimate. April's increase was revised to 0.4% from 0.5%. Sales were up 6.9% from a year earlier, retail trade gained 1.0% on the month, and nonstore sales rose 12.2% annually. The release reinforced the picture of resilient spending even as higher financing costs weighed on housing.

The oil story ran in the other direction. Crude remained sharply lower over the week on prospects for restored Hormuz flows, and 10-year breakevens fell again. Wednesday's inventory data showed a nearer-term supply constraint, however: commercial stocks dropped 8.3 million barrels, the Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell 8.9 million, and refinery inputs climbed to 17.192 million barrels a day. Those draws helped keep oil sensitive to disruptions even as markets priced eventual normalization.

Bill yields increasingly reflected the prospective policy path. The 13-week rose 5 basis points to 3.77%, the 26-week 11 to 3.91%, and the 52-week 14 to 3.98%; very short tenors moved just 1 basis point. The sharper rise farther along the bill curve matched the new rate expectations more closely than an immediate shortage of cash.

The $69 billion 119-day auction cleared at a 3.670% high discount rate, equivalent to a 3.767% investment rate. Bid-to-cover was 2.87, with 11.86% of bids at the high rate allotted. Of $68.459 billion in competitive awards, indirect bidders received $36.282 billion, direct bidders $3.486 billion and dealers $28.691 billion. No prior-auction or when-issued comparison was supplied. Settlement on June 23 will bring the associated cash movement after the holiday.

## Financing Continues, With Strong Borrowers Getting Better Terms

HDFC Bank priced a $750 million 5-year dollar bond at 90 basis points over Treasuries, its tightest new-issue spread. Orders exceeded $1.3 billion, enabling a 30-basis-point tightening from initial guidance. The bank's previous $750 million sale in February 2024 had priced its 3- and 5-year tranches at 95 and 108 basis points, respectively; the latest 5-year came 18 basis points inside that comparison.

The improvement came despite a 21% slide in HDFC shares this year and scrutiny following its chairman's resignation. India's central bank said it found no material conduct concern. The bond order book showed investors remained willing to extend credit to the country's largest private lender even amid an equity governance controversy.

Transport issuers also benefited from an open market. Athens International Airport raised €500 million in its euro-bond debut, pricing a 7-year issue at 98 basis points over mid-swaps. TAP Air Portugal began investor calls for a proposed €300 million 5-year speculative-grade bond as the government pursued the sale of a 49.9% stake. Airlines and airports have issued more than $10.5 billion this year, their largest first-half total since 2021. More than $22 billion of aviation debt sold in 2020–21 carried 5- to 7-year maturities, making replacement of pandemic-era financing a large part of the current calendar. TAP's calls were still preliminary, unlike Athens' completed sale.

Lenovo used its share price to raise $2 billion through zero-coupon convertibles due in 2033. The 47.5% conversion premium was within a marketed 40%-50% range. Proceeds will fund refinancing and share repurchases, including purchases of outstanding 2029 convertibles at 293.2% of principal. Existing holders, convertible specialists and long-only funds participated. The structure saves cash interest while leaving the possibility of future equity dilution.

Nassau County Tobacco Settlement Corp. provided the week's starkest contrast to the successful refinancings. It missed a $36 million payment due at the start of June, the first default in an approximately $80 billion municipal-bond sector backed by cigarette-settlement receipts. Cigarette shipments have declined for years, weakening the payments behind securities issued more than two decades ago. Similar bonds fell following the missed payment. This was a deterioration in the underlying collateral, rather than a result of Wednesday's change in Treasury yields.

The ECB separately raised an operating-risk concern around AI adoption. Christine Lagarde said wider use could concentrate financial exposures and increase cyber vulnerabilities. The ECB had tested 109 banks against a severe cyberattack and planned to write to chief executives about resilience and investment needs. These were supervisory concerns and future costs, rather than reported credit losses from AI.

Listed credit funds moved down with stocks and Treasuries: LQD lost 0.32%, HYG 0.37% and JNK 0.38%. Their returns were less informative about individual borrowers than the strong HDFC and Athens order books, Lenovo's convertible terms and the tobacco-bond default.

## Europe and Japan Keep Their Own Policy Questions Open

Euro-area inflation remained broad even after oil retreated. May headline inflation was confirmed at 3.2% from a year earlier, up from 3.0%, while core accelerated to 2.6% from 2.2%. Services rose 3.5%, contributing 1.61 percentage points to the annual rate, and energy contributed 0.98 point. Investors still expected at least another 25-basis-point ECB increase, taking the deposit rate to 2.5%.

ECB officials warned that damaged infrastructure, restocking and wage responses could prolong the effects of high energy prices. Their wage tracker points to 2.6% annual pay growth in the second half, well below the 5.2% peak in 2024 but firmer than in the first half. Lower spot crude offers time to assess the shock; the services and wage data are why officials have not declared it over.

Sweden held at 1.75% for a sixth meeting but raised its assessment of the chance of an increase later in 2026. Underlying inflation was low, activity weaker than normal and May unemployment 9.4%. Even so, the projected rate path reached 2% in the final quarter of 2027. The decision retained patience for now while shifting the medium-term path higher.

In the UK, headline inflation held at 2.8% in May instead of reaching the 3% estimate. The 10-year gilt yield fell 5 basis points to 4.74%, its lowest in two months. Services inflation, however, rose more than expected to 3.7%. The Bank of England was expected to hold its 3.75% rate on June 18, with services prices still central to what comes next.

Japan's June 16 hike remained a point of comparison for global investors. Long JGB yields edged higher, and 90% of 44 economists surveyed on June 17 expected another increase by December. December was the most common choice, followed by October; the median expected peak rate rose to 1.75%. The BOJ's plan to stop actively reducing monthly bond purchases from April 2027 may steady the supply outlook, but Japanese investors still face a higher domestic policy rate and bond yields than before the latest decision.

China, meanwhile, changed how it intends to manage short-term liquidity. The central bank signaled a future move toward an overnight policy-rate framework, narrowed its corridor around market borrowing costs to 50 basis points from 70, and created a facility for foreign official institutions to obtain yuan against government bonds. These are changes to the funding framework, with implications for the usefulness of Chinese bonds as collateral; they were not a conventional rate move on Wednesday.

## South Africa's Inflation Surprise, Then Brazil's Cut

South African consumer inflation rose to 4.5% in May from 4.0%, the highest in almost two years, but came in below the 4.7% survey estimate. Core inflation accelerated to 3.8% from 3.6%. Contracts reduced the amount of tightening expected by November to 25 basis points from 34, implying a policy-rate peak of 7.25%. The softer surprise gave investors some relief despite inflation remaining above the central bank's 3% objective.

Brazil cut its Selic rate by 25 basis points to 14.25% after the 17:00 ET New York fixed-income cutoff, its third consecutive reduction. The central bank warned that growth and inflation had both accelerated and that fiscal stimulus might add further price pressure. Inflation was above the tolerance range and expectations above the 3% target. Extending the target horizon to early 2028 allowed the cut, but guidance left an August pause possible.

The dollar strengthened with US short rates, adding to the cost of unhedged external liabilities. The yen also weakened to about 160.80 per dollar, reviving concern about intervention and a reversal of carry positions. Japanese authorities had deployed a record ¥11.73 trillion from late April through late May. That history explains why investors remained alert to sharp currency moves, though Wednesday did not show a discrete seizure of dollar funding.

EMB fell 0.40% as dollar rates rose. South Africa's pricing response and Brazil's later decision show why the fund move cannot stand in for every local policy or sovereign credit change.

## Stocks Fall as the Dollar Rises; Semiconductors Are an Exception

The S&P 500 fell 1.21% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.99% as higher real yields weighed on risk assets. VIX jumped 12.37% to 18.44. Semiconductor shares bucked the broader decline, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 1.38%. The exception matters after two days of large moves in chip stocks, but does not make the overall equity session positive.

The dollar index rose 0.55% to 100.09, consistent with the shift in relative policy expectations. WTI rebounded 0.97% to $76.79 and Brent added 0.75% to $79.55; each was still down about 14.5% over a week and roughly 27% over a month. The daily oil bounce and large inventory draws left immediate supply risks visible, while lower 10-year breakevens showed that Treasury investors continued to price some benefit from a future Hormuz reopening.

Gold gained 0.65% to $4,358.90 despite the stronger dollar and higher real yields, though it was down 4.32% over a month. Its daily gain did not establish a single explanation for investor positioning. Across markets, the strongest common signal was the rise in US policy-sensitive yields and the dollar; oil and semiconductors did not move in the same direction as broad equities.

## Thursday's Data and Auctions Arrive Before the Holiday

Initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey are due June 18 at 08:30 ET. The previous readings were 229,000 claims and -0.4 for the regional index. The releases will give the first new evidence on labor and factory activity after the Fed raised its inflation forecasts and traders moved toward pricing an October hike.

Central-bank decisions follow in a compressed window: Switzerland at 03:30 ET, Norway at 04:00 and the UK at 07:00. Holds are the baseline for all three, while surveys anticipated 25-basis-point increases from Bank Indonesia and the Philippine central bank. Their votes and guidance, alongside currencies, will show how policy makers are responding to the energy shock and its partial reversal.

Developments reported after the 17:00 New York fixed-income cutoff already informed the Asian handoff. Taiwan held at 2% for a ninth consecutive quarter but described its stance as hawkish, raising its 2026 growth forecast to 9.45% from 7.28% and projecting 1.91% inflation. New Zealand reported 0.8% first-quarter growth after a revised 0.5% in the fourth quarter; swaps put an 80% chance on an RBNZ quarter-point increase on July 8. These releases belong to the next regional discussion, rather than the explanation for the completed US close.

Treasury auctions $70 billion of 4-week and $75 billion of 8-week bills at 11:30 ET on June 18, followed by a $24 billion reopening of the 1.25% 5-year TIPS at 13:00. Bidder participation, TIPS pricing and short-term cash rates will be especially useful immediately after the Fed decision, before the full June 19 fixed-income closure.
